text:
Which of the following statements are TRUE about Haloform reaction?

A. Sodium hypochlorite reacts with KI to give KOI .

B. KOI is a reducing agent.

C. $α,β$-unsaturated methylketone 
[IMG]

iodoform reaction.

D. Isopropyl alcohol will not give iodoform test.

E. Methanoic acid will give positive iodoform test.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) This statement is true. Sodium hypochlorite oxidises iodide ion to hypoiodite. So, the reaction is:

$\mathrm{NaOCl}+\mathrm{KI}\to \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{KOI}$

(B) This statement is false. $\mathrm{KOI}$ (hypoiodite) behaves as an oxidising agent in haloform (iodoform) conditions, not as a reducing agent.

(C) This statement is true. In iodoform reaction, any compound having a $-\mathrm{COCH}_{3}$ (methyl ketone) group gives iodoform test. An $α,β$-unsaturated methyl ketone still contains the $-\mathrm{COCH}_{3}$ group, so it gives iodoform reaction.


[IMG]


gives iodoform reaction.

(D) This statement is false. Isopropyl alcohol $(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CHOHCH}_{3})$ gives iodoform test because it is oxidised (in presence of $\mathrm{I}_{2}/\mathrm{NaOH}$) to acetone $(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}_{3})$, which is a methyl ketone.

(E) This statement is false. Methanoic acid $(\mathrm{HCOOH})$ does not have the required $-\mathrm{COCH}_{3}$ group (or the $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-$ group) for iodoform test, so it does not give a positive iodoform test.

text: The oxidation state of chromium in the final product formed in the reaction between KI and acidified $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ solution is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In acidified $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$, chromium is in the $+6$ oxidation state (in $\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$).

When $\mathrm{KI}$ is added in acidic medium, $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ is oxidised to $\mathrm{I}_{2}$ and dichromate is reduced to $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$.

Reduction half-reaction (NCERT method):

$\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}+14\mathrm{H}^{+}+6\mathrm{e}^{-}\to 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+7\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

So, chromium in the final product is $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$, i.e. oxidation state is $+3$.

Correct option: B ($+3$)

text: In Carius method 0.2425 g of an organic compound gave 0.5253 g silver chloride. The percentage of chlorine in the organic compound is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass of organic compound taken $=0.2425\text{g}$

Mass of $\text{AgCl}$ obtained $=0.5253\text{g}$

In Carius method for estimation of halogens, the halogen present in the organic compound is converted into silver halide. Here chlorine is obtained as $\text{AgCl}$.

In $\text{AgCl}$, the fraction of chlorine is:

$\frac{\text{Atomic mass of Cl}}{\text{Molar mass of AgCl}}=\frac{35.5}{143.5}$

So, mass of chlorine in $0.5253\text{g}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ is:

$\frac{35.5}{143.5}\times 0.5253$

Therefore, percentage of chlorine in the compound is:

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Percentage of}\mathrm{Cl}=\dfrac{35.5}{143.5}\times \dfrac{0.5253}{0.2425}\times 100 \\ =53.58% \end{array}$

solution.body:
Zn removes the two vicinal Br atoms, so the C=C forms between the two carbons that carried Br: a cyclopentene whose two allylic carbons carry an ethyl group and a methyl group respectively.

$\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ from HBr adds to one alkene carbon and leaves a secondary carbocation next to the CH bearing the alkyl group; a 1,2-hydride shift from that CH gives a tertiary carbocation on the alkyl-bearing ring carbon.

The tertiary carbocation on the methyl-bearing carbon has 7 $α$-hydrogens (3 from $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ and 2 from each ring $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$), while the one on the ethyl-bearing carbon has 6 (2 from the ethyl $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ and 2 from each ring $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$). Greater hyperconjugation makes the methyl-bearing cation the more stable one, and it is formed preferentially.

$\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ attacks this carbocation, giving 1-bromo-3-ethyl-1-methylcyclopentane, with Br and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ on the same ring carbon and the ethyl group 1,3 to it.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

Given above is the concentration vs time plot for a dissociation reaction : $\mathrm{A}\to \mathrm{nB}$.

Based on the data of the initial phase of the reaction (initial 10 min ), the value of n is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the graph, in the first $10$ minutes the concentration of $\mathrm{A}$ decreases from $0.05$ to $0.04$.

So, amount of $\mathrm{A}$ dissociated in $10$ minutes $=0.05-0.04=0.01$.

For the reaction $\mathrm{A}\to \mathrm{nB}$, when $0.01$ of $\mathrm{A}$ reacts, $\mathrm{B}$ formed $=0.01\times n$.

From the graph, in the same time interval, concentration of $\mathrm{B}$ formed becomes $0.03$. So we equate $0.01\times n$ to $0.03$ and find $n$.

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{A}\to \mathrm{nB} \\ 0.05 0 \\ 0.04 0.01\times \mathrm{n} \\ 0.01\times \mathrm{n}=0.03 \\ \mathrm{n}=3 \end{array}$

text:
Observe the following reactions at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$.

I. $\mathrm{A}\to$ products.

II. $5\mathrm{Br}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{BrO}_{3}{}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+6\mathrm{H}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})\to 3\mathrm{Br}_{2}(\mathrm{aq})+3\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$

Both the reactions are started at 10.00 am . The rates of these reactions at 10.10 am are same. The value of $-\frac{\Delta \left [\mathrm{Br}^{-}\right ]}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}$ at 10.10 am is $2\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\min ^{-1}$. The concentration of A at 10.10 am is $10^{-2}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$. What is the first order rate constant (in $\min ^{-1}$ ) of reaction $I$ ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At $t=10$ minutes (i.e., at 10:10 am)

For reaction II, $5\mathrm{Br}^{-}$ are consumed when the reaction proceeds once. So, the rate of reaction is related to the rate of decrease of $\left [\mathrm{Br}^{-}\right ]$ as:

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Rate of reaction}=-\dfrac{1}{5}\dfrac{\Delta \left [\mathrm{Br}^{-}\right ]}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\dfrac{1}{5}\times \left (2\times 10^{-4}\right ) \\ =4\times 10^{-5} \end{array}$

Now consider reaction I: $\mathrm{A}\to$ products.

At $t=10$ minutes, both reactions have the same rate. So, the rate of reaction I at this time is also $4\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\min ^{-1}$.

Since reaction I is first order, its rate law is:

Rate of reaction $=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}]$

Given $[\mathrm{A}]=10^{-2}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$ at 10:10 am, we write:

Rate of reaction $=4\times 10^{-5}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}]$

So,

$\mathrm{k}=\frac{4\times 10^{-5}}{10^{-2}}=4\times 10^{-3}\min ^{-1}.$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: The work functions of two metals $(\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}\qquad$ and $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}})$ are in the $1:2$ ratio. When these metals are exposed to photons of energy 6 eV , the kinetic energy of liberated electrons of $M_{A}:M_{B}$ is in the ratio of $2.642:1$. The work functions (in eV ) of $M_{A}$ and $M_{B}$ are respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the work functions be $𝜙_{A}$ and $𝜙_{B}$.

Given ratio of work functions:

$𝜙_{A}:𝜙_{B}=1:2\Rightarrow 𝜙_{B}=2𝜙_{A}$

Photon energy is $hν=6\text{eV}$.

By Einstein’s photoelectric equation:

$K_{\max }=hν-𝜙$

So,

$K_{A}=6-𝜙_{A}$

$K_{B}=6-𝜙_{B}=6-2𝜙_{A}$

Given,

$\frac{K_{A}}{K_{B}}=\frac{2.642}{1}=2.642$

So,

$\frac{6-𝜙_{A}}{6-2𝜙_{A}}=2.642$

Cross-multiplying:

$6-𝜙_{A}=2.642(6-2𝜙_{A})$

$6-𝜙_{A}=15.852-5.284𝜙_{A}$

Bring like terms together:

$5.284𝜙_{A}-𝜙_{A}=15.852-6$

$4.284𝜙_{A}=9.852$

$𝜙_{A}=\frac{9.852}{4.284}\approx 2.3\text{eV}$

Then,

$𝜙_{B}=2𝜙_{A}\approx 4.6\text{eV}$

Answer: $2.3\text{eV},4.6\text{eV}$ (Option C)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
Iodoform test can differentiate between

A. Methanol and Ethanol

B. $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}$ and $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$

C. Cyclohexene and cyclohexanone

D. Diethyl ether and Pentan-3-one

E. Anisole and acetone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The Iodoform Test
The iodoform test is used to detect the presence of a specific structural group in a molecule. A compound gives a positive iodoform test if it contains either:

A methyl ketone group ($CH_{3}-C(=O)-$ group)

An alcohol group that can be oxidized to a methyl ketone. This means the alcohol must have a $CH_{3}-CH(OH)-$ group.

A positive test is indicated by the formation of a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($CHI_{3}$) when the compound is warmed with iodine ($I_{2}$) and an aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide ($NaOH$).

The general reaction is:

$R-CO-CH_{3}\leftarrow ^{I_{2},NaOH}CHI_{3}↓+R-COONa$

(Yellow ppt)

Now, let's analyze each pair of compounds one by one.

A. Methanol ($CH_{3}OH$) and Ethanol ($CH_{3}CH_{2}OH$)

Methanol ($CH_{3}OH$): This is a primary alcohol. It does not have the required $CH_{3}-CH(OH)-$ group. Therefore, Methanol gives a negative iodoform test.

Ethanol ($CH_{3}CH_{2}OH$): This is the only primary alcohol that gives a positive iodoform test. Under the reaction conditions, ethanol is first oxidized to acetaldehyde ($CH_{3}CHO$). Acetaldehyde has a methyl ketone group ($CH_{3}-C(=O)-$H). Thus, Ethanol gives a positive iodoform test.

Since one gives a positive test and the other gives a negative test, they can be differentiated.

B. Acetic acid ($CH_{3}COOH$) and Propanoic acid ($CH_{3}CH_{2}COOH$)

Carboxylic acids do not give the iodoform test. The acidic proton of the $-COOH$ group reacts with the base ($NaOH$), but the resulting carboxylate ion does not undergo iodination like ketones do.

Therefore, both Acetic acid and Propanoic acid give a negative iodoform test.

Since both give a negative test, they cannot be differentiated.

C. Cyclohexene and Cyclohexanone

Cyclohexene: This is an alkene. It does not have a methyl ketone group or an alcohol group. It gives a negative iodoform test.

Cyclohexanone: This is a ketone, but it does not have a methyl ($CH_{3}$) group attached to the carbonyl ($C=O$) group. The structure is $-CH_{2}-C(=O)-CH_{2}-$. Therefore, it gives a negative iodoform test.

Since both give a negative test, they cannot be differentiated.

D. Diethyl ether ($CH_{3}CH_{2}-O-CH_{2}CH_{3}$) and Pentan-3-one ($CH_{3}CH_{2}-C(=O)-CH_{2}CH_{3}$)

Diethyl ether: Ethers do not have the required structural groups for this test. It gives a negative iodoform test.

Pentan-3-one: This is a ketone, but the carbonyl group is bonded to two ethyl ($CH_{3}CH_{2}-$) groups, not a methyl group. Therefore, it gives a negative iodoform test.

Since both give a negative test, they cannot be differentiated.

E. Anisole ($C_{6}H_{5}-O-CH_{3}$) and Acetone ($CH_{3}-C(=O)-CH_{3}$)

Anisole: This is an ether. It does not have the required structural group. It gives a negative iodoform test.

Acetone (Propanone): This is a methyl ketone. It has the $CH_{3}-C(=O)-$ group. Therefore, it gives a positive iodoform test.

Since one gives a positive test and the other gives a negative test, they can be differentiated.

Conclusion

Based on our analysis, the iodoform test can be used to differentiate the pairs in A and E.

Therefore, the correct choice is Option C: A & E Only.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : $(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{3}\mathrm{C}^{⊕}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{C}^{⊕}\mathrm{H}_{3}$ as nine hyperconjugation interactions are possible in $(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{3}\mathrm{C}^{⊕}$.

Statement II : $\mathrm{C}^{⊕}\mathrm{H}_{3}$ is less stable than $(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{3}\mathrm{C}^{⊕}$ as only three hyperconjugation interactions are possible in $\mathrm{C}^{⊕}\mathrm{H}_{3}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hyperconjugation in a carbocation is the delocalisation of a $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ $σ$ bond on a carbon adjacent to the positive carbon into its empty p orbital; the number of hyperconjugation interactions equals the number of $α$-hydrogens.

In $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}{}^{+}$ the positive carbon carries three $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ groups, giving $3\times 3=9$ $α$-hydrogens, so nine hyperconjugation interactions stabilise it and it is far more stable than $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}{}^{+}$. Statement I is true.

In $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}{}^{+}$ no carbon is attached to the positive carbon; its three hydrogens are on the charged carbon itself, so no hyperconjugation is possible. $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}{}^{+}$ is indeed less stable, but the reason given (three hyperconjugation interactions) is wrong, so Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: A mixed ether $(\mathrm{P})$, when heated with excess of hot concentrated hydrogen iodide produces two different alkyl iodides which when treated with aq. NaOH give compounds $(\mathrm{Q})$ and $(\mathrm{R})$. Both $(\mathrm{Q})$ and $(\mathrm{R})$ give yellow precipitate with NaOI . Identify the mixed ether $(\mathrm{P})$ :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Excess hot concentrated $\mathrm{HI}$ cleaves an ether and converts both alkyl groups into alkyl iodides; aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ then gives the two alcohols Q and R.

NaOI gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform only with alcohols containing the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH}){}^{-}$ group (ethanol included), so both alkyl groups of P must give such alcohols.

Option (B) is ethyl sec-butyl ether: it gives ethyl iodide and 2-iodobutane, which hydrolyse to ethanol (Q) and butan-2-ol (R), and both give iodoform.


[IMG]

In (A), (C) and (D) one of the two alcohols, 1-phenylpropan-1-ol, benzyl alcohol and 2-methylbutan-2-ol respectively, lacks the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH}){}^{-}$ group, so only one alcohol gives the test.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The second ionisation enthalpy of Na is larger than the corresponding ionisation enthalpy of Mg .

Statement II : The ionic radius of $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ is larger than that of $\mathrm{F}^{-}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I:  

Na: $1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{1}$  

After first ionisation, $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ becomes $1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}$ (noble gas configuration).  

So, the second ionisation enthalpy of Na means removing an electron from a stable noble gas core, which needs very high energy.

Mg: $1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}$  

After first ionisation, $\mathrm{Mg}^{+}$ becomes $1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{1}$.  

So, the second ionisation enthalpy of Mg removes the remaining valence $3s$ electron, which needs less energy than removing from a noble gas core.

Hence, $IE_{2}(\mathrm{Na})>IE_{2}(\mathrm{Mg})$.  

So, Statement I is true.

Statement II:  

$\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ has $8+2=10$ electrons, and $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ has $9+1=10$ electrons.  

So, $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ are isoelectronic (same number of electrons).

In an isoelectronic series, ionic radius decreases as nuclear charge ($Z$) increases, because higher $Z$ pulls electrons more strongly.

Here, $Z(\mathrm{O})=8$ and $Z(\mathrm{F})=9$.  

So, $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ (higher $Z$) will be smaller than $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$.

Therefore, $r(\mathrm{O}^{2-})>r(\mathrm{F}^{-})$.  

So, Statement II is true.

Correct option: Option C
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: A student has been given a compound " $x$ " of molecular formula- $\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{7}\mathrm{N}$. ' $x$ ' is sparingly soluble in water. However, on addition of dilute mineral acid, ' $x$ ' becomes soluble in water. ' $x$ ' when treated with $\mathrm{CHCl}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{KOH}(\mathrm{alc})$, ' $y$ ' is produced. ' $y$ ' has a specific unpleasant smell. On treatment with benzenesulphonyl chloride, ' $x$ ' gives a compound ' $z$ ' which is soluble in alkali. The number of different " H " atoms present in ' z ' is:-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{7}\mathrm{N}$ is sparingly soluble in water but dissolves in dilute acid, so it is a basic amine. It gives a foul-smelling isocyanide with $\mathrm{CHCl}{}_{3}$ and alcoholic KOH (carbylamine reaction), so it is a $1^{\circ }$ amine: x is aniline, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, and y is phenyl isocyanide, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NC}$.


[IMG]

With benzenesulphonyl chloride, aniline gives z, N-phenylbenzenesulphonamide $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}\mathrm{NHC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$, whose acidic $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ makes it soluble in alkali.


[IMG]

z has 11 hydrogen atoms in all, but they are of 7 different kinds: in the ring attached to S, ortho (2 H), meta (2 H) and para (1 H) are 3 kinds; in the ring attached to N, ortho, meta and para are another 3 kinds; the $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ hydrogen is the seventh.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

Identify the INCORRECT statements from the following :

A. Notation ${}_{12}^{24}\mathrm{Mg}$ represents 24 protons and 12 neutrons.

B. Wavelength of a radiation of frequency $4.5\times 10^{15}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ is $6.7\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{m}$.

C. One radiation has wavelength $=λ_{1}(900\mathrm{nm})$ and energy $=\mathrm{E}_{1}$. Other radiation has wavelength $=λ_{2}(300\mathrm{nm})$ and energy $=\mathrm{E}_{2}$. $\mathrm{E}_{1}:\mathrm{E}_{2}=3:1$.

D. Number of photons of light of wavelength 2000 pm that provides 1 J of energy is $1.006\times 10^{16}$.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement A
For ${}_{12}^{24}\mathrm{Mg}$:

Atomic number $Z=12$ $\Rightarrow$ number of protons $=12$

Mass number $A=24$ $\Rightarrow$ protons + neutrons $=24$

So, neutrons $=24-12=12$.

Given statement says 24 protons and 12 neutrons, which is wrong.  

✅ A is incorrect

Statement B
Wavelength $λ$ is given by

$λ=\frac{c}{ν}$

Here $c=3\times 10^{8}\text{m s}^{-1}$ and $ν=4.5\times 10^{15}\text{s}^{-1}$

$λ=\frac{3\times 10^{8}}{4.5\times 10^{15}}=0.6667\times 10^{-7}=6.67\times 10^{-8}\text{m}$

Matches the given value.  

✅ B is correct

Statement C
Energy of radiation:

$E=\frac{hc}{λ}\Rightarrow E\propto \frac{1}{λ}$

So,

$\frac{E_{1}}{E_{2}}=\frac{λ_{2}}{λ_{1}}=\frac{300}{900}=\frac{1}{3}$

Therefore,

$E_{1}:E_{2}=1:3$

But given is $E_{1}:E_{2}=3:1$, which is wrong.  

✅ C is incorrect

Statement D
Energy per photon:

$E=\frac{hc}{λ}$

Given $λ=2000\text{pm}=2000\times 10^{-12}=2\times 10^{-9}\text{m}$

$E=\frac{(6.626\times 10^{-34})(3\times 10^{8})}{2\times 10^{-9}}=9.939\times 10^{-17}\text{J}$

Number of photons for $1\text{J}$:

$N=\frac{1}{9.939\times 10^{-17}}=1.006\times 10^{16}$

Matches the given value.  

✅ D is correct

Incorrect statements: A and C only
Correct option: Option B

text:
Which statements are NOT TRUE about $\mathrm{XeO}_{2}\mathrm{F}_{2}$?

A. It has a see-saw shape.

B. Xe has 5 electron pairs in its valence shell in $\mathrm{XeO}_{2}\mathrm{F}_{2}$.

C. The $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{Xe}-\mathrm{O}$ bond angle is close to $180^{\circ }$.

D. The $\mathrm{F}-\mathrm{Xe}-\mathrm{F}$ bond angle is close to $180^{\circ }$.

E. Xe has 16 valence electrons in $\mathrm{XeO}_{2}\mathrm{F}_{2}$.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{XeO}{}_{2}\mathrm{F}{}_{2}$, Xe (8 valence electrons) forms two Xe=O double bonds and two Xe–F single bonds and keeps one lone pair, so its valence shell holds 4 σ bond pairs, 2 π bond pairs and 1 lone pair: 7 electron pairs, or 14 electrons.

The 4 σ bond pairs and the lone pair take a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement with the lone pair and both O atoms equatorial, so the shape is see-saw: A is true.

Xe has 7, not 5, electron pairs in its valence shell: B is not true.

The equatorial O–Xe–O angle is about $105^{\circ }$, far from $180^{\circ }$: C is not true.

The axial F–Xe–F angle is about $174^{\circ }$, close to $180^{\circ }$: D is true.

Xe has 14, not 16, valence electrons: E is not true.

The statements that are not true are B, C and E.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
It is noticed that $\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{Pb}^{4+}$ but $\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}$ is less stable than $\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$. Observe the following reactions.

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{PbO}_{2}+\mathrm{Pb}\to 2\mathrm{PbO};\Delta _{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{G}^{\circ }(1) \\ \mathrm{SnO}_{2}+\mathrm{Sn}\to 2\mathrm{SnO};\Delta _{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{G}^{\circ }(2) \end{array}$

Identify the correct set from the following
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{PbO}_{2}+\mathrm{Pb}\to 2\mathrm{PbO}$

In this reaction, lead changes from $+4$ (in $\mathrm{PbO}_{2}$) and $0$ (in $\mathrm{Pb}$) to $+2$ (in $\mathrm{PbO}$).

Since $\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{Pb}^{4+}$, the reaction prefers to form $\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}$.

So, this reaction is spontaneous, hence $\Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ }(1)$ is negative.

$\mathrm{SnO}_{2}+\mathrm{Sn}\to 2\mathrm{SnO}$

In this reaction, tin changes from $+4$ (in $\mathrm{SnO}_{2}$) and $0$ (in $\mathrm{Sn}$) to $+2$ (in $\mathrm{SnO}$).

But $\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}$ is less stable than $\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$, so forming $\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}$ is not preferred.

Therefore, this reaction is non-spontaneous, hence $\Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ }(2)$ is positive.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
Identify the CORRECT set of details from the following :

A. $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{3+}$ : Inner orbital complex; $\mathrm{d}^{2}\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridized

B. $[\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-}$ : Outer orbital complex; $\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{2}$ hybridized

C. $[\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-}$ : Outer orbital complex; $\mathrm{d}^{2}\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridized

D. $[\mathrm{FeF}_{6}]^{3-}$ : Outer orbital complex; $\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{2}$ hybridized

E. $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}$ : Inner orbital complex; $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridized

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{6}$; $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ pairs the electrons as $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, leaving two 3d orbitals empty, so $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$ is an inner orbital complex with $d^{2}sp^{3}$ hybridisation. Correct.

B: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{4}$; $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs, the four 3d electrons stay unpaired and the 4d orbitals are used, giving an outer orbital complex with $sp^{3}d^{2}$ hybridisation. Correct.

C: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{6}$) with weak field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ is high spin with 4 unpaired electrons, so $[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ is an outer orbital complex with $sp^{3}d^{2}$, not $d^{2}sp^{3}$, hybridisation. Incorrect.

D: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$; with weak field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ all five electrons stay unpaired, so $[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ is an outer orbital complex with $sp^{3}d^{2}$ hybridisation. Correct.

E: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$; strong field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs the electrons into four 3d orbitals, leaving one 3d orbital empty, so $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ is a square planar inner orbital complex with $dsp^{2}$, not $sp^{3}$, hybridisation. Incorrect.

The correct set is A, B and D only.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Elements X and Y belong to Group 15. The difference between the electronegativity values of ' X ' and phosphorus is higher than that of the difference between phosphorus and ' Y '. ' X ' & ' Y ' are respectively
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As per the NCERT textbook, electronegativity is the ability of an atom to attract a shared pair of electrons. For Group 15, the electronegativity decreases as we go down the group.

Let's look at their approximate electronegativity values (on the Pauling scale):

$EN(N)=3.0$

$EN(P)=2.1$

$EN(As)=2.0$

$EN(Sb)=1.9$

$EN(Bi)=1.9$

Notice a very important point: The drop in electronegativity from Nitrogen (N) to Phosphorus (P) is very large ($3.0-2.1=0.9$). However, for the elements below Phosphorus, the values decrease very slowly.

The question states: "The difference between the electronegativity values of 'X' and phosphorus is higher than that of the difference between phosphorus and 'Y'."

Let's write this mathematically. Let $EN$ stand for electronegativity. The absolute difference is what matters.

$|EN(X)-EN(P)|>|EN(P)-EN(Y)|$

This means we are looking for an element 'X' whose electronegativity is very different from Phosphorus, and an element 'Y' whose electronegativity is very close to Phosphorus.

Now, let's check each option using the electronegativity values.

Option A: X = As & Y = Bi

Difference 1: $|EN(X)-EN(P)|=|EN(As)-EN(P)|=|2.0-2.1|=0.1$

Difference 2: $|EN(P)-EN(Y)|=|EN(P)-EN(Bi)|=|2.1-1.9|=0.2$

Is $0.1>0.2$? No. So, this option is incorrect.

Option B: X = Bi & Y = N

Difference 1: $|EN(X)-EN(P)|=|EN(Bi)-EN(P)|=|1.9-2.1|=0.2$

Difference 2: $|EN(P)-EN(Y)|=|EN(P)-EN(N)|=|2.1-3.0|=0.9$

Is $0.2>0.9$? No. So, this option is incorrect.

Option C: X = N & Y = As

Difference 1: $|EN(X)-EN(P)|=|EN(N)-EN(P)|=|3.0-2.1|=0.9$

Difference 2: $|EN(P)-EN(Y)|=|EN(P)-EN(As)|=|2.1-2.0|=0.1$

Is $0.9>0.1$? Yes. This matches the condition given in the question.

Option D: X = As & Y = Sb

Difference 1: $|EN(X)-EN(P)|=|EN(As)-EN(P)|=|2.0-2.1|=0.1$

Difference 2: $|EN(P)-EN(Y)|=|EN(P)-EN(Sb)|=|2.1-1.9|=0.2$

Is $0.1>0.2$? No. So, this option is incorrect.

Therefore, X is Nitrogen (N) and Y is Arsenic (As).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

Consider the following reaction of benzene.


[IMG]

In compound $(Q)$, the percentage of oxygen is $____$ %. (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene with $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COCl}$ (anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$) gives the 1,4-diketone P, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$.

With aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ on heating, the enolate of the terminal $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ group attacks the benzoyl carbonyl carbon (intramolecular aldol), closing a five-membered ring; dehydration gives the conjugated enone Q, 3-phenylcyclopent-2-en-1-one, $\mathrm{C}{}_{11}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}\mathrm{O}$.


[IMG]

$M(\mathrm{C}{}_{11}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}\mathrm{O})=11(12)+10(1)+16=158\text{g mol}^{-1}$

$%\text{O}=\dfrac{16}{158}\times 100=10.13%$

Hence, the answer is 10.

text:
Total number of unpaired electrons present in the central metal atoms/ions of 

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}],[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}]^{2-},[\mathrm{PtCl}_{2}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{2}],[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}$ and $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}$ is $____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{0}$ is $3d^{8}4s^{2}$; strong-field CO pairs all ten electrons into $3d^{10}$ and Ni uses $sp^{3}$ (tetrahedral), so there are 0 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$; weak-field $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ causes no pairing and Ni uses $sp^{3}$ (tetrahedral), so there are 2 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{PtCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{2}]$: $\mathrm{Pt}{}^{2+}$ is $5d^{8}$; a 5d $d^{8}$ ion forms a square planar $dsp^{2}$ complex with all eight electrons paired, so there are 0 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$; strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs the electrons and Ni uses $dsp^{2}$ (square planar), so there are 0 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Pt}{}^{2+}$ is $5d^{8}$ with $dsp^{2}$ (square planar), so there are 0 unpaired electrons.

$\text{Total}=0+2+0+0+0=2$

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
200 cc of $x\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{M}$ potassium dichromate is required to oxidise 750 cc of 0.6 M Mohr's salt solution in acidic medium.

Here $x=$ $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In acidic medium, dichromate oxidises $Fe^{2+}$ to $Fe^{3+}$.

Half-reactions (NCERT method):

$Cr_{2}O_{7}^{2-}+14H^{+}+6e^{-}\to 2Cr^{3+}+7H_{2}O$

$Fe^{2+}\to Fe^{3+}+e^{-}$

So, $1$ mole of $Cr_{2}O_{7}^{2-}$ oxidises $6$ moles of $Fe^{2+}$.

Step 1: Moles of $Fe^{2+}$ in Mohr’s salt solution
Volume $=750\text{cc}=0.75\text{L}$, Molarity $=0.6\text{M}$

$n(Fe^{2+})=0.75\times 0.6=0.45\text{mol}$

Step 2: Moles of $K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7}$ required
$n(K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7})=\frac{0.45}{6}=0.075\text{mol}$

Step 3: Use given dichromate solution data
Volume $=200\text{cc}=0.2\text{L}$, Molarity $=x\times 10^{-3}\text{M}$

$n=0.2\times x\times 10^{-3}=2\times 10^{-4}x$

Equate moles:

$2\times 10^{-4}x=0.075$

$x=\frac{0.075}{2\times 10^{-4}}=375$

$x=375$

text:
$\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌2\mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$

$\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ and $\mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ are added to a 1 L flask and it is found that the system attains the above equilibrium at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$ with the number of moles of $\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{g}),\mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ and $\mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$ being 3,3 and 9 mol respectively (equilibrium moles). Under this condition of equilibrium, 10 mol of $\mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$ is added to the flask and the temperature is maintained at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$. Then the number of moles of $\mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$ in the flask when the new equilibrium is established is $____$ . (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given reaction:

$\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌2\mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$

1) Find $K_{c}$ from the first equilibrium
At equilibrium in a $1\mathrm{L}$ flask:

$[\mathrm{X}_{2}]=3,[\mathrm{Y}_{2}]=3,[\mathrm{Z}]=9$

$K_{c}=\frac{[\mathrm{Z}]^{2}}{[\mathrm{X}_{2}][\mathrm{Y}_{2}]}=\frac{9^{2}}{3\times 3}=\frac{81}{9}=9$

2) After adding $10$ mol of $Z$
New moles immediately (before shift):

$\mathrm{X}_{2}=3,\mathrm{Y}_{2}=3,\mathrm{Z}=9+10=19$

Since $Z$ is added, equilibrium shifts left. Let the backward reaction proceed by $x$ moles:

$\mathrm{X}_{2}$ increases by $x$

$\mathrm{Y}_{2}$ increases by $x$

$\mathrm{Z}$ decreases by $2x$

So at new equilibrium:

$[\mathrm{X}_{2}]=3+x,[\mathrm{Y}_{2}]=3+x,[\mathrm{Z}]=19-2x$

3) Apply equilibrium constant again
$K_{c}=\frac{(19-2x)^{2}}{(3+x)(3+x)}=9$

$(19-2x)^{2}=9(3+x)^{2}$

Taking positive square root (concentrations are positive):

$19-2x=3(3+x)=9+3x$

$19-9=3x+2x$

$10=5x\Rightarrow x=2$

Hence,

$\text{New moles of}Z=19-2(2)=19-4=15$

Nearest integer = $15$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution. At 320 K , the vapour pressure of the solution, containing 3 mol of $A$ and 1 mol of $B$ is 500 mm Hg . At the same temperature, if 1 mol of A is further added to this solution, vapour pressure of the solution increases by 20 mm Hg . Vapour pressure (in mm Hg ) of B in pure state is $____$ . (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an ideal solution, by Raoult’s law:

$P_{\text{total}}=x_{A}P_{A}^{0}+x_{B}P_{B}^{0}$

First solution (3 mol $A$, 1 mol $B$)
Total moles $=3+1=4$

$x_{A}=\frac{3}{4},x_{B}=\frac{1}{4}$

Given $P_{\text{total}}=500$ mm Hg:

$500=\frac{3}{4}P_{A}^{0}+\frac{1}{4}P_{B}^{0}$

Multiply by 4:

$2000=3P_{A}^{0}+P_{B}^{0}...(1)$

After adding 1 mol $A$ (4 mol $A$, 1 mol $B$)
Total moles $=4+1=5$

$x_{A}=\frac{4}{5},x_{B}=\frac{1}{5}$

New vapour pressure $=500+20=520$ mm Hg:

$520=\frac{4}{5}P_{A}^{0}+\frac{1}{5}P_{B}^{0}$

Multiply by 5:

$2600=4P_{A}^{0}+P_{B}^{0}...(2)$

Solve
Subtract (1) from (2):

$2600-2000=(4P_{A}^{0}+P_{B}^{0})-(3P_{A}^{0}+P_{B}^{0})$

$600=P_{A}^{0}$

Put in (1):

$2000=3(600)+P_{B}^{0}=1800+P_{B}^{0}$

$P_{B}^{0}=200\text{mm Hg}$

Answer: $200$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift
